summary: Former music hustler Tony Alamo and his wife Susan built an apocalyptic Christian cult in California and Arkansas, using unpaid child labor for a celebrity denim jacket line while Tony took child brides, until his 2009 conviction.

evidence.note: Tony born Bernie Lazar Hoffman in Joplin, Missouri, 1934; Susan's Arkansas birth follows
Susan's recurring con of posing as a missionary to collect church offerings
Tony and Susan meet in a Los Angeles bar around 1966 while each tries to con the other
foundation established 1969 to take in street youth and their wages
compound bought in Saugus, California, in 1971
after Susan's cancer diagnosis the cult moves to a compound in Dyer, Arkansas
Susan dies 1982; followers ordered to pray over her embalmed body for months
rhinestone jacket brand sold to celebrities, decorated by unpaid cult children
Labor Department suit from 1976 ends in a unanimous Supreme Court ruling on cult wages
arrested in Florida in 1994 and jailed for tax fraud, released 1998, moves to Fouke
2008 raid, 2009 conviction for transporting girls across state lines, dies in prison 2017

notes: Susan Alamo's birth year transcribed ambiguously; 1925 used from own knowledge. Her life is a long Part 1 segment, so it opens covered_span. Arkansas and California share the story, so both subdivisions are listed. labor-exploitation and slavery-forced-labor both apply (unpaid child labor plus the federal wage case). Racist bus hoax and John Birch Society are a short Part 1 segment, left out of themes. Victims of the sexual abuse are mostly minors, so sexual-abuse omitted.
